meta.purpose: MATCHFIX: (A) LanceDB recall matching to <=0.004 with a fine knob-pair search; (B) like-for-like same-order rebuild non-determinism floors for pgvector and LanceDB in the current 3-seed/200-episode protocol; (C) honest per-setting sweep values.

engines.lancedb: LanceDB 0.40.0 (lancedb python package; Rust lance engine)

protocol.operator: embedding <-> query::vector  (the L2 operator for a vector_l2_ops index)

task_B.pgvector: rebuild the SAME generation twice: identical id-order heap, identical build parameters, no permutation, then compare the two top-10 sets.  Runs: CREATE INDEX vs REINDEX, REINDEX vs REINDEX (parallel), and 1st vs 2nd REINDEX with max_parallel_maintenance_workers=0 (serial).  200 episodes.
task_B.lancedb: two engine rebuilds of the SAME non-reordered data (post-optimize() vs create_index(replace=True)); a second optimize() is a no-op so it cannot supply the second rebuild.

deviations: Sweep values are EXTRACTED from results_engine_multiseed.json (no new computation); raw per_episode is carried over unchanged.
LanceDB's table.optimize() is idempotent on unchanged data, so the LanceDB same-order floor uses create_index(replace=True) for the second rebuild (the routine optimize() invokes).
LanceDB exposes no HNSW adjacency: only the answer-level any-difference convention is measurable there.
limitations: pgvector floor uses the id-order (clean) heap, matching generation A of the paper's engine experiment.
LanceDB has no server-side multi-tenant story; it is an embedded library.
